defect.description: The setting is read as settings['FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE'] or False instead of settings.getbool(...): command-line overrides arrive as text, so -s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False (or =0) gives the non-empty string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on.

review_items: feedstorage.py:27 - FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE read with `or False` instead of getbool; CLI string 'False' is truthy and enables active mode
feedstorage.py:29-38 - FTP connection not wrapped in try/finally; quit skipped on exception
tests/test_feedstorage.py:16-18 - test only uses native bool, not CLI string path
votes.evidence_quote: `settings["FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE"] or False` does not convert the CLI string value to bool. `Settings.from_command_line` (src/settings.py:27) stores `-s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False` as the raw string `"False"`, and `"False" or False` evaluates to the truthy string `"False"`, so `self.active` becomes `"False"` and `if self.active:` on line 34 erroneously enables active mode when the user requested passive.
votes.justification: The first finding names the exact faulty expression in from_settings. It gives the cause: CLI values arrive as strings, so 'False' is truthy. It also recommends the getbool fix.
